title: Behind the Camera
about: A thank-you to Joy for the years she spent helping State Arts-In run and for capturing the ordinary Prep Week moments that became lasting memories.
description: Joy was part of my 4-H and State Arts-In world for as long as I can remember. One of the things I associate most strongly with her is seeing her around Prep Week with a camera, catching whatever we happened to be doing for the daily slideshow. Some of those pictures preserved moments I still remember clearly: sanding nearly two inches off a board while practically falling asleep, working from inside one of the light boxes, and becoming part of the improvised solution when a platform leg needed more weight to reach the floor. I originally remembered another photo too, though that memory has since disappeared, which is part of why those pictures matter. Joy's role went far beyond taking photos. She was there throughout my participant years and later became one of the people Assistant Directors could turn to, along with Kirsten, when decisions or problems needed someone with more experience. This song is about both sides of that memory: Joy behind the camera preserving the small moments, and Joy behind the program helping make State Arts-In happen.
lyrics: Verse 1
You were there before I started,
Though I couldn't tell you when
You first became a face I knew
Through 4-H way back then.
And when I came to State Arts-In,
You were already part of it,
Another constant in the building,
Helping all the pieces fit.
Pre-Chorus
But some of what I remember best
Isn't meetings, shows, or plans.
It's seeing you come wandering through
With a camera in your hands.
Chorus
Behind the camera,
Catching moments as they came,
Little pieces of our Prep Week
That might otherwise have changed.
Nothing staged or picture-perfect,
Just whatever we were doing then.
Behind the camera,
You caught pieces I still remember when
I think of State Arts-In.
Verse 2
Space Year needed one board sanded,
Two whole inches out somehow.
So I settled into sanding
Till the edge was evened out.
Simple work became a rhythm,
Half awake but carrying on,
Somehow sanding while half sleeping—
And your camera caught it all.
Then those light boxes we were building
Turned to prisons for a while.
I was working from inside one
When you found me by the aisle.
Coming down the stairs, you saw me,
Caught the scene for everyone:
Tech Crew's newest box-bound prisoner,
Still just trying to get things done.
Chorus
Behind the camera,
Catching moments as they came,
Little pieces of our Prep Week
That would make the slideshow later that day.
Nothing staged or picture-perfect,
Just whatever we were doing then.
Behind the camera,
You caught pieces I still remember when
I think of State Arts-In.
Verse 3
Then a platform leg needed lowering,
Wouldn't quite come to the floor.
So apparently the proper tool
Was a couple people more.
No machine and no invention,
Just some bodies adding weight.
I became part of construction—
Tech Crew engineering at its greatest.
And somewhere there's another moment,
At least I know there used to be.
I remembered four when I started,
Now there's only these three.
Maybe that's the thing with memories:
Some stay sharp and some move on.
That's why someone with a camera
Can matter after years are gone.
Bridge
But you were more than all the pictures,
More than slides at end of day.
You were there throughout my years there,
Helping guide things on their way.
And when I became an AD,
When decisions needed more,
You and Kirsten were the people
We could bring those questions toward.
During Prep Week through the building,
During fair week on the floor,
There were always things that needed
Someone watching something more.
Final Chorus
Behind the camera,
You were part of every year,
Sometimes somewhere in the background,
But somehow always there.
From the pictures to the program,
From the building to the show,
There are people in a story
Who become part of what you know.
Behind the camera,
You saved moments I still see.
Little pieces of State Arts-In,
Little pieces now of me.
Outro
I don't have one giant story,
Or one moment that says it all.
Just years of seeing you around there,
Through Prep Week and through the halls.
So Joy, for all the years you gave it,
And the moments you helped us save,
There's a place for you within these songs
For one simple reason:
I wanted you that way.
